races.name: Dickie McGuinness Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beauvallon
runners_data.note: W P Mullins-trained four-year-old with back-to-back wins at 16f on Good and Soft, stepping back up to an appropriate trip here; Brian Hayes retains the ride and two wins from six runs in similar conditions is the strongest form line in the race, though the hold-up style requires something to go wrong up front.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins, the latest a comfortable success at Punchestown, leave this gelding well fancied to complete the hat-trick; that form has since been boosted and the stable's strength suggests more to come off just a short break, though this deeper field is the obvious test.

runners_data.name: Karlynn
runners_data.note: Recent winner at 20f on Good ground gives John M Burke's runner rock-solid course-condition credentials; E Walsh rides and the prominent style means Karlynn should slot in right behind Tex Amare without a fight, making this one of the better-placed horses in the expected race shape.
runners_data.comment: A comfortable Wexford success last time, achieved on a step up in trip, points to physical progress, and today's trip and ground both look within range; a moderate run of form before that leaves this gelding with questions to answer at this level.

runners_data.name: Evangelic
runners_data.note: RK Watson's lightly-raced four-year-old has struggled in open company with a form string of 700, and while it is a natural hold-up horse, the crowded rear means it has been pushed into a midfield position it would not naturally choose — STYLE_FIT 0.91 applies and its recent finishing positions in Good-ground races offer little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Yet to threaten in its last three starts for a new yard, with the latest effort at Punchestown hinting the trip stretched its stamina; sporting a first-time hood and best around 7f, conditions here look a stretch given the modest recent form.

runners_data.name: Mino Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Second Mullins runner, equipped with a tongue tie and showing consistent placed form at 16f; Josh Williamson claims 5lb and a prominent style suits the anticipated race shape well, though the lack of a win and a 90-day absence since last seen are mild flags in a novice context.
runners_data.comment: Successful in bumpers in France, this gelding was worn down late after a mistake-strewn round, finishing second beaten 10 lengths at Cork last time, though that form has since been boosted. A first-time tongue-tie and a powerful stable add appeal despite a modest hurdles tally.

runners_data.name: Pebble Island
runners_data.note: John C McConnell's gelding has not run for 203 days and carries a 14F tag indicating a significant layoff; a natural rear-of-field type that has been placed into midfield here by necessity — STYLE_FIT 0.90 — and the combination of a lengthy break, inexperience over hurdles (form 6U-), and race-shape mismatch makes it hard to construct a winning case.
runners_data.comment: An inconsistent sort across both codes, this gelding unseated last time out and has a little to prove on recent evidence, though conditions and trip both look suitable; a yard short on winners and a mixed profile make it hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Puppet Master
runners_data.note: Ciaran Murphy's runner has one career win from twelve career hurdle runs, all on Good ground, but has not appeared for 190 days and carries a 42F flag; genuinely a hold-up horse by style, the redistribution to midfield is an unwanted compromise, and while the Good-ground win is a small positive, STYLE_FIT 0.92 and the long absence keep expectations measured.
runners_data.comment: Successful in a Listed race on the Flat, this gelding should enjoy a return to hurdles and a shorter trip after finding a stiff 12-furlong test at The Curragh beyond him last time. A first-time tongue-tie may help, with adapting back to timber the only thing to prove.

runners_data.name: Yup Bro
runners_data.note: Tagged with a fading-in-finish flag and a form figure of just 0 on its sole run for McConnell; a hold-up horse whose finishing record across five career runs — all poor — and a recent heavy beat in similar going conditions (20d since last run on a 14F marker) makes it the most straightforwardly exposed runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Switching disciplines could be the making of this gelding, since modest Flat form may not reflect his potential over hurdles, and he is among the more highly rated here for that reason. A below-par run down the field last time and a yard short on winners, though, temper the enthusiasm somewhat.

runners_data.name: Tex Amare
runners_data.note: Anthony Mullins's only previous run showed a third at 16f on Soft, suggesting it handles cut but is untested on Good; as the lone front-runner it holds enormous positional control and Dylan O'Connor (7lb claim) keeps the weight attractive, though novice jumping reliability under pressure at the business end is the one genuine query.
runners_data.comment: A promising debut third, beaten 13 lengths in a maiden hurdle at Roscommon, hints this filly has more to offer, backed up by useful placed form on the level in Germany; a first-time hood may help, but the modest rating leaves her hard to fancy from this rank.

races.paceDynamic: Tex Amare is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner novice hurdle and, with no rival likely to seriously contest that position, should dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the outset over the 2m1f Bellewstown circuit on Good ground. Beauvallon, Puppet Master, Pebble Island, and Evangelic are all genuine hold-up horses by nature, but the field contains more closers than the map can accommodate at the rear — Puppet Master, Pebble Island, and Evangelic have been redistributed to midfield because they cannot all settle in their preferred backmarker role; in practice, Karlynn and Mino Des Mottes are best placed to press Tex Amare from prominent positions. With only one true pace-setter and a sustainable tempo likely, the race shape should suit horses who can travel prominently close to the early fractions and produce a clean jump at the second-last, giving Tex Amare every chance to control and convert, while prominent-to-midfield profiles with proven Good-ground form get the best of conditions. A lone, uncontested front-runner on Good ground over a fair test strongly favours the lead-to-prominent profile — a horse who can sit just off Tex Amare and pounce from the second-last is the primary beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tex Amare's jumping closely at the second-last and last — if Dylan O'Connor's 7lb claimer gets into trouble at a hurdle having controlled the race, the lead advantage evaporates instantly and a prominent stalker like Karlynn will punish it.

Beauvallon is the classiest horse on paper but needs a strong pace or a late blunder from the leaders to get into this from the rear — if Tex Amare sets a genuinely slow tempo, Brian Hayes may find Beauvallon with nowhere near enough to close on a fresh Tex Amare.

Puppet Master, Pebble Island, and Evangelic are all being asked to race in a more forward position than they would naturally choose — monitor at the early stages whether any of them drift back further than the map suggests, which would effectively take them out of contention entirely.

Mino Des Mottes returns after 90 days with a tongue tie; watch the market move in the hour before the race — if Mullins's second string drifts sharply, it may indicate the yard's confidence sits with Beauvallon rather than here.

Yup Bro's fading-in-finish tag and McConnell's dual runner (alongside Pebble Island) make it worth monitoring for any market activity — a significant gamble would be a noteworthy anomaly given its exposed and modest profile.

races.name: Grimme Ireland Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Laxxio
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Anthony Mullins who has placed twice in similar Good-ground conditions; 77 days off is notable but the form string shows consistency, and a prominent berth on a Good-tracking day suits the profile well.
runners_data.comment: Fitness is the obvious question given a fall and a below-par run among recent starts, but this gelding showed promise when third, beaten 5 1/2 lengths, at Bellewstown last time, fresh from just a short break; conditions and trip both look suitable if he stays sound.

runners_data.name: Loyal Touch
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type whose last five runs have all come from the rear and produced finishes of 6th or worse; 51 days off with a flat-racing query (24F tag) and the expected steady tempo is not generous to this style.
runners_data.comment: Poor recent form has followed this gelding to a new yard, and a below-par effort at Limerick last time did little to inspire; a fair mark on UK form offers hope, with today's trip and ground in his favour, but he has yet to settle since the move.

runners_data.name: Press The Button
runners_data.note: Placed on Good at 2m and a winner over hurdles on similar ground; Keith Donoghue's booking is significant and the tongue-strap is already worn — the prominent style is perfectly aligned with what this race is expected to deliver.
runners_data.comment: A promising hurdling debut at Ballinrobe, filling the runner-up spot beaten 6 1/2 lengths after a break, points to more improvement now fully tuned up. Conditions and trip both suit, and cheekpieces go on for the first time, with only limited experience over hurdles the slight concern.

runners_data.name: Whats New
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed 3rd twice on Good going at 2m1f; Cian Quirke is a claiming jockey and the trainer has modest recent form (T14: 2/30), but the horse's own consistency on the right ground type gives it relevance in a race that suits the prominent profile.
runners_data.comment: A frustrating sort at times, this gelding failed to complete when running out last time at Clonmel, but he has otherwise been a fairly reliable frame-filler over hurdles; conditions and trip both look suitable, with jumping cleanly the main thing needed to see more.

runners_data.name: Pepper Noir
runners_data.note: Returning from a 537-day absence (70 flat runs tag) and has only experience on Flat tracks and Good ground at shorter trips; the tongue-tie is worn but the layoff, the amateur jockey, and the step into hurdles from this background is a very big ask.
runners_data.comment: Out of sorts on the level recently, with a below-par run at Navan last time doing nothing to change that, this mare has plenty to prove back over hurdles; a first-time tongue-tie and only a short break offer some hope, though the recent form gives little to go on.

runners_data.name: Allroadsleadtorome
runners_data.note: Recently ran 9th and 7th in two Good-ground 2m3f races; has been slotted into midfield because the hold-up berths are over-subscribed in this field, meaning Shane Fitzsimons (7) will need to adapt his ride — the style-fit discount is real and the recent form is modest.
runners_data.comment: Modest efforts have followed this gelding's hurdling debut, with the Downpatrick run last time showing little progress; a yard without a winner recently adds to the concerns, though he does act well on heavy and today's conditions and trip suit. More time looks needed before he's competitive.

runners_data.name: Highland Realm
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Willie Mullins runner with a single run showing a 2nd on Good ground; the 323-day absence is the risk, but the form and stable suggest a prominent berth is likely and he is well-qualified for this shape if fit.
runners_data.comment: A narrow runner-up on his only start, beaten half a length in a bumper at Tramore, this gelding was sent off favourite but had to settle for second. A lengthy absence since is the concern, but a powerful stable suggests more to come now switching to hurdles, with conditions and trip both suiting.

runners_data.name: Hopeful Hero
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent, placing in 6 of his last 10 runs on Good or similar going at this type of trip; rides for a small yard with no recent form (T14: 0/0) but the horse itself is the story — the prominent-to-midfield profile is second nature to him.
runners_data.comment: Consistency is the calling card, with frame finishes including third, beaten 3 1/4 lengths, at Sligo last time continuing a pattern set since a solid debut defeat by a useful rival. Conditions look no obstacle, and a first-time hood may help find the finishing effort still missing.

runners_data.name: Million Dollar Man
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner; form reads poorly (P-60) and he did trail home 21st and 6th in his last two, but the key here is he dictates the pace rather than wins it — his tactical role is more influential than his chance of winning.
runners_data.comment: A drop in trip did this gelding no favours at Punchestown last time, where the pace proved too hot down the field; he looks better suited by further and more of a fit for handicaps. A return to a stiffer trip is likely needed to show his real form.

runners_data.name: Paymelater
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with a string of mid-pack finishes on Good ground but no wins and no places in his last five; 20 days ago and no trainer form (T14: 0/0) — unlikely to benefit unless the pace unexpectedly collapses.
runners_data.comment: A modest hurdling debut at Downpatrick, hampered by jumping errors, leaves this gelding needing to bounce back, with inconsistent bumper form before that offering little encouragement either; conditions and trip both look fine, but there is little in the book yet to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Kasper Hauser
runners_data.note: The 2nd in a 2m1f Good-ground race last time out is the headline form angle; his natural hold-up style means he has been pushed into midfield by redistribution, and his chance depends on getting a clean run rather than being able to dictate his own tempo.
runners_data.comment: On his best form this gelding carries a fair mark, but there's no hiding from a well-held effort in a handicap at Kilbeggan last time. Conditions and trip both suit, and he's fresh from just a short break, though he needs to rediscover that form to feature.

runners_data.name: Matcho d'Agrostis
runners_data.note: Two falls in recent starts are a major concern for market confidence regardless of style; the "fades in finish" flag plus an amateur jockey and minimal usable form make this one hard to trust at this level.
runners_data.comment: Two fallen finishes preceded a well-beaten run at Punchestown last time, painting a difficult recent picture, even though his debut form has since been boosted at a higher level. He still has plenty to prove and looks more of a fit for a lowly handicap than a factor here.

runners_data.name: The Flying Rambler
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with one run showing 7th on Good; the "lightly raced" flag and an unclassified style mean there is genuine uncertainty about where he settles — Conor Stone-Walsh is not a high-profile booking to fill in the blanks.
runners_data.comment: Racing too keenly proved the undoing of this gelding on his only start, a well-beaten bumper run here, and there's plenty to find educationally now switching to hurdles. A first-time hood may aid settling, and he's fresh from just a short break, but the concerns are obvious.

runners_data.name: Wackestone
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy is a significant jockey booking for Gordon Elliott, and the 2nd from three runs on Good is the best form reference available; 89 days off is a concern but the yard often produces horses ready first time back, and a midfield position could serve him in a compressed race.
runners_data.comment: A below-par effort last time out follows a game third, beaten just a length, in a conditions event at The Curragh that shows this gelding can mix it at a good level, and cut in the ground should suit. First-time cheekpieces and a powerful stable add interest, though he can be tricky to fathom.

runners_data.name: Double Order
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up type whose "fades in finish" flag and redistribution into midfield signal that the expected race shape is not in his favour; form on Good is poor (3 runs, 3 mid-pack finishes) and the style mismatch materially reduces his chance.
runners_data.comment: A below-par effort up in trip down the field in a bumper at Wexford last time leaves plenty to find on this mare's hurdling debut, and conditions alone won't be enough to turn things round; she remains an unknown quantity at best on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Getaway Tobin
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by John McConnell who has placed 5th and 4th in his last two on Good at 2m; 21 days ago and a clear-run scenario in midfield is needed — the trainer has two other runners in this race which complicates stable tactics.
runners_data.comment: Modest bumper form, capped by a well-held run at Hexham last time, gives little to work with for this mare's switch to hurdles, though earlier flickers of promise suggest more may follow. A first-time tongue-tie and suitable conditions offer some hope, but a yard short on winners doesn't help.

runners_data.name: G N Jefferson
runners_data.note: Fades in finish flag backed up by a single run showing 12th on Good; Tom Buckley and Jack Teal are a low-profile combination and there is little evidence to suggest this horse copes with the trip or tempo.
runners_data.comment: A modest introduction down the field in an amateur riders' bumper at Aintree last time leaves this gelding needing to step forward on both his point-to-point and bumper form. He's fresh from just a short break, but there's little in the book yet to inspire real confidence.

runners_data.name: Willows Word
runners_data.note: Debut runner with no form, unknown going preference, lightly raced flag and an amateur jockey — impossible to assess beyond noting that 19-runner maiden hurdles are a tough starting point; going listed as UNKNOWN.
runners_data.comment: A daughter of Poet's Word making her debut, this filly is a half-sister to Shirley's The Boss, who found 16 furlongs too far, and the stable isn't renowned for a strong hit-rate under rules. With no bumper experience behind her, she looks one to watch rather than back with confidence.

runners_data.name: Sunny Dude
runners_data.note: The "fades in finish" flag is damning given a form string showing 0 and a history of bottom-half finishes in large fields; Good ground and a big field look like precisely the conditions that expose the limitations highlighted in his record.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten effort on his hurdling debut at Ballinrobe last time gives little encouragement, and this gelding otherwise looks up against stronger rivals on this form; his best form to date has come around 13 furlongs, so today's test remains an open question rather than a formality.

races.paceDynamic: Million Dollar Man is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 19 and, with no genuine pace rival likely to challenge him from the outset, he can bowl along at whatever tempo suits him — a sustainable, unhurried gallop is the most probable outcome on Good ground over 2m1f. Press The Button and Highland Realm are the most likely horses to sit close behind him in the prominent positions, with Laxxio and Hopeful Hero also likely to dispute early ground, creating a compact racing head to the field but without the friction that comes from a contested lead. The field holds more hold-up types than can all settle at the rear — Double Order, Allroadsleadtorome, and Kasper Hauser are genuine closers redistributed into the midfield picture because the true hold-up berths are over-subscribed; their ability to close late is compromised by a moderate early tempo that compresses the field. A steady, uncontested gallop on Good turf at Bellewstown favours horses who travel prominently, have the jump technique to settle into a rhythm, and can sustain a run from two out — the prominent-to-midfield profile wins this race shape.

watchPoints.text: Million Dollar Man's early tempo is the race's most critical variable — if Ben Harvey lets him stride out even fractionally faster than a hack, the compression that suits prominent horses is broken and a chaotic shape emerges behind him.

Wackestone's jockey booking (Jack Kennedy, Gordon Elliott) is significantly above the market expectation for this horse and deserves close pre-race monitoring — market moves here should be treated seriously.

John McConnell saddles three runners (Allroadsleadtorome, Pepper Noir, Getaway Tobin) and stable tactics could influence where each settles — watch paddock behaviour and early positioning for signs of a stable plan.

Kasper Hauser's redistribution into midfield masks a genuine placed run at 2m1f on Good ground last time — if he somehow secures closer than expected to the pace in a 19-runner field, his chance is materially higher than his mapped position implies.

With 19 runners and only one genuine front-runner, the jump at the first hurdle is a congestion flashpoint — any prominent horse that gets shuffled back in the early scramble effectively loses its positional advantage in a shape that is built around travelling up with the pace.

races.name: Street Sweep Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Becasse
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's five-year-old showed solid form finishing second on Good ground (2/16f) most recently and has two wins/places from four starts in similar conditions — a natural midfield-to-rear operator who has been further pushed back in the map to fill the hold-up role; the key question is whether she can generate enough of a run in a 19-runner field from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: A narrow defeat off a lower mark at Listowel last time, beaten just half a length, keeps this gelding firmly involved on solid recent form including a win among his last four. The yard is in good form and a first-time tongue-tie adds appeal on a fair mark, though he must prove he can turn placed efforts into victories at this level.

runners_data.name: Fiver Friday
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's six-year-old has an excellent record on Good ground (13/15 starts, two wins six places) and won over this 17f trip — 77 days off with a flat run on his return, but the Good ground and a prominent position here suit his profile ideally.
runners_data.comment: A useful mare in both codes, she was successful by 4 1/4 lengths off a much lower mark last time out. Now racing off a career-high rating, a well-beaten run on the level three starts back under a stiffer mark is a mild concern, though conditions and trip suit.

runners_data.name: Ifiwerearichman
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's eight-year-old is a two-time winner on Good ground (8/15 form) and placed over this 17f trip — racing with a prominent headgear flag, and the apprentice claim from Alan O'Sullivan (5lb) is a meaningful weight relief in this handicap context.
runners_data.comment: A mixed recent record, including a pulled-up run and a fall, is balanced by a solid third, beaten 4 1/4 lengths, in a rated event at Wexford last time, fresh from a break. Conditions and trip both suit, first-time cheekpieces may sharpen him, and there should be more to come.

runners_data.name: Barbizon
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner and will have the lead entirely to himself — he won twice earlier in the campaign but has weakened in both subsequent starts (6th, 4th, then pulled up in softer), and the style-fit flag (0.93) reflects he is racing in a natural but high-risk position; 116 days off adds uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: A progressive sort on the Flat, this gelding found a stiff mark too strong in a juvenile handicap hurdle at Cheltenham last time, but he drops back in company today for a powerful stable. A first-time tongue-tie and time off add slight uncertainty, though he rates among the leading players.

runners_data.name: Encanto Bruno
runners_data.note: John McConnell's eight-year-old has placed at 2/16f and 2/20f on Good ground in recent runs and carries an apprentice (Dylan Kidd, 7lb), giving a useful weight advantage — his style is genuinely prominent, which puts him in the thick of the prominent traffic, though the trainer's 0-from-29 in the last 14 days is a dampener.
runners_data.comment: A modest run of finishes includes a well-held effort at Kilbeggan last time, where racing too freely took its toll on stamina; today's drop back in trip could suit a formerly useful sort, and ground on the sounder side is needed, though a yard short on winners doesn't inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Putapoundinthejar
runners_data.note: A J Martin's six-year-old returned with a third on Good ground (3/16f) most recently and has proven ability at this trip — shown as prominent in a genuinely prominent-heavy field, so must find room and position early; trainer has had limited recent activity (0/4 last 14 days).
runners_data.comment: A success by half a length off a much lower mark here in April has since been backed up by a solid third, beaten 4 lengths, off the same mark last time. Conditions and trip both suit, and this gelding looks capable of better again with more positive tactics.

runners_data.name: Spy
runners_data.note: C Byrnes' seven-year-old is a recent winner on Good ground (1/16f last time) and carries the hg:p flag — his prominent style fits the map naturally, and two wins from 11 Good-ground runs suggests he fires consistently in these conditions; the 5lb claim from Williamson adds to the appeal.
runners_data.comment: Back to form since getting off the mark over hurdles, this gelding was suited by better ground when winning a handicap at Listowel last time. Conditions and trip both suit again, and first-time cheekpieces add interest, though he rates only the outsider of this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Autumn Twist
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's five-year-old is a natural prominent racer whose position has been displaced to midfield because the field cannot accommodate so many pace-committed horses — the style-fit flag (0.92) reflects a real risk of racing out of role after 67 days off, and recent finishing positions of 9th, 6th, 6th on Good ground are unencouraging.
runners_data.comment: A mixed recent record for this gelding includes a below-par effort at Limerick last time, where going too soon proved costly, though a win is also among his last five starts; conditions look suitable, but climbing too high in the weights back over hurdles is the obvious concern here.

runners_data.name: Lisnamult Lad
runners_data.note: Ian Donoghue's nine-year-old has a string of pull-up and fall results (FP9P-P) with no recent placed effort on Good ground — the amateur rider (7lb claim) helps in weight terms, but the form profile is deeply concerning and his prominent placement in the map masks a runner who has been struggling to complete.
runners_data.comment: A run of setbacks, capped by failing to complete in a handicap hurdle at Kilbeggan last time, leaves this gelding with plenty to prove, and he may be better suited by fences long-term. Front-running tactics play to his strengths and first-time cheekpieces could help, but stamina beyond 2 1/2 miles remains unproven.

runners_data.name: Red Glory
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's eight-year-old won two back on Good ground (1/16f) and has placed six times in similar conditions from 12 efforts — the Good-ground track record (3 wins, 6 places from 12) is the standout stat here, and he carries the hg:t flag suggesting he's suited when freshened; 20 days since last run is fine.
runners_data.comment: A win among his last five starts underpins this gelding, and he did well to hold his position at Downpatrick last time, back from a break, before one proved too good. Conditions look suitable and a first-time tongue-tie is fitted, but he otherwise rates towards the back of this field on official figures.

runners_data.name: Come On The Lads
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's six-year-old (hg:p) is a natural prominent runner who cannot secure that position in this large field and has been mapped to midfield — the style-fit warning (0.93) is real, and a 17th and 7th in two of his last three on Good ground undermines confidence despite his SOF win.
runners_data.comment: A useful sort in both codes, this gelding's fair hurdles mark looks the more promising context after a below-par Flat return down the field at The Curragh last time; conditions look suitable, and a win remains among his last five starts, with first-time cheekpieces added for this switch back.

runners_data.name: Malbay Madness
runners_data.note: Dermot McLoughlin's six-year-old carries a hold-up headgear flag and has won twice very recently (1/18f, 1/16f on Good), making him arguably the form pick in the race — he has been further redistributed to the rear of the map to fill the hold-up section, but his natural style is at least pace-flexible, and back-to-back wins on this ground are hard to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins feature among this gelding's last five starts, the latest a comfortable success by 4 lengths off a lower mark at Downpatrick, and there's scope for more physical progress yet. Conditions and trip both suit and a first-time hood is added, though he rates only a modest chance on official figures.

runners_data.name: Missus Beeton
runners_data.note: J P Dempsey's eight-year-old is a natural prominent racer pushed rearward in the map due to overcrowding — all five recent runs came on Soft ground, making the Good surface here a genuine question mark (10/15 form record on Good is modest: one win, five places), and 91 days off adds to the fitness uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: A generally consistent mare with two wins among her last five starts, she found the level too high when well beaten in a valuable handicap at Fairyhouse last time. Conditions and trip both suit, and she's fresh from just a short break, though her mark looks to have crept above her true level.

runners_data.name: Thisistheway
runners_data.note: Yvonne Latta's seven-year-old has placed at 2/20f and 3/23f on Good ground and is a genuine prominent-style horse bumped into the midfield section by the overcrowded field — with a style-fit flag of 0.92 and 63 days off, there is risk he never gets into the race from a position he is unaccustomed to running from.
runners_data.comment: A leading contender on class, this mare was travelling like the one to beat when falling in a Listed handicap hurdle at Punchestown last time, and that placed form marks her out as progressive and well treated. Decent ground suits, she's fresh from just a short break, and the fall remains her only recent blemish.

runners_data.name: Stuntman Steve
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's seven-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse (natural H style, hg:b) who gets his true position in the map — his last two runs were non-completions (P, U) and the form string shows decline, but for a scenario where the pace compresses and a late run is possible, he is one of the few authentic hold-up types in the field.
runners_data.comment: A mixed campaign continues for this gelding, who failed to complete after unseating in a handicap chase at Punchestown last time; blinkers go on for the first time as connections switch back to hurdles, though a stiff mark and unproven stamina for this longer trip leave obvious questions.

runners_data.name: Playtime
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old is a natural prominent racer displaced to midfield — second last time on Good ground (2/16f) is creditable and Jack Kennedy's booking is a strong positive signal, but a style-fit of 0.93 means if he can't reclaim a prominent spot, Kennedy's class advantage may be neutralised.
runners_data.comment: A consistent sort who found only 4 1/4 lengths too much when runner-up in a novice hurdle at Punchestown last time, this gelding carries a mark that already demands plenty, and a win features among his last five starts; conditions and trip both suit, though the stable is currently short on winners.

runners_data.name: Paul's Dream
runners_data.note: Anthony Mullins' seven-year-old won last time (1/16f GOO) and has three wins from 10 Good-ground starts — a genuine prominent horse pushed into midfield on the map, with a 0.91 style-fit warning; if he recaptures a forward position he has obvious claims, but the redistribution limits confidence.
runners_data.comment: Two wins feature among this mare's last five starts, the latest an easy success by 8 lengths off a lower mark after dropping in grade at Ballinrobe, and she looks well treated on the strength of previous graded form. Conditions here suit, though a fall earlier this campaign and the step up in company today leave a little still to prove.

runners_data.name: Fast Felix
runners_data.note: Eoin McCarthy's eight-year-old has an excellent Good-ground profile (14/15 starts in similar conditions, two wins four places) and the 7lb claim from Thomas O'Connor is useful — he is naturally prominent but mapped to midfield with a 0.93 style-fit flag, and while his adaptability across going types is a positive, he has to overcome the positional challenge.
runners_data.comment: A well-beaten effort in a handicap hurdle at Listowel last time continues a modest recent run, and there's a sense his mark already reflects his form. Conditions and trip both suit and a first-time tongue-tie is added, but little in recent starts inspires much confidence.

runners_data.name: Minella Post
runners_data.note: Thomas Gibney's seven-year-old has no jockey listed, limited recent form (14th last time at 20f Good), and modest Good-ground profile (4 from 6 runs, no wins, one place) — the long 66-day absence and uncertain jockey booking make this a difficult proposition in a competitive 19-runner field.
runners_data.comment: A needed run showed in this gelding's last start, ridden too prominently down the field in a handicap hurdle at Punchestown, though that experience should sharpen him for today. A fairly consistent sort in maidens who may do better now handicapping, he returns from just a short break with a first-time tongue-tie, but he still rates near the bottom of this field.

races.paceDynamic: Barbizon is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, critically, is uncontested for the lead — with no other genuine pace-setter to push him, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m1f Good ground trip. The field is heavily loaded with prominent types (Fiver Friday, Ifiwerearichman, Red Glory, Spy, Encanto Bruno, Putapoundinthejar among others), meaning the space directly behind Barbizon will be intensely competitive, but the pace itself will not be pressured from outside. Several runners flagged as prominent — Autumn Twist, Thisistheway, Missus Beeton, Come On The Lads, Playtime, Paul's Dream, Fast Felix — cannot all secure their natural position in this field shape and have been displaced rearward in the map; those who fail to find prominent ground early will be racing out of role. This race shape, with a lone front-runner setting a controlled tempo on Good ground in a large field, strongly favours horses who can race close to the pace in the first four or five and sustain their effort — true prominent types with proven form on Good ground have the clearest tactical advantage, while genuine hold-up horses face the double jeopardy of a moderate gallop and a big field to navigate.

runners_data.name: Bold Reflection
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent racer with a win over 16f on Heavy ground but a worrying tendency to fade in the finish; 27 days since last run and a John McConnell yard out of form (0/27 in 14 days) make this hard to trust over an extended 2m4½f.|
runners_data.comment: A bumper winner, this mare's form has dipped over hurdles, mistakes contributing to a well-beaten effort at Punchestown last time. Two miles on softer ground should suit, and connections were successful in this race a year ago, but she needs to recapture that bumper-winning spark now over hurdles to feature.

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner ridden by Jack Kennedy for the in-form Gordon Elliott yard (11/49 T14); five runs on similar going with two placed efforts suggest a genuine staying front-runner, though a fall last time is worth noting.|
runners_data.comment: Considered a leading threat, she was below her best in an under-par third, beaten ten lengths at Downpatrick last time. Suited by two miles three on yielding and sporting a first-time hood, though repeating that recent dip would be the obvious concern up in this company.

runners_data.name: Chisel Hill
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with a placed run over 20f on Good ground; Ian Donoghue's yard is cold (0/17 T14) and 37 days since last run is a minor flag, but course-distance form gives this a solid ground profile.|
runners_data.comment: Race-fit and rated competitive after finishing second, beaten six and a half lengths, at Limerick last time following a drop in grade. Effective at two miles three on heavy and with today's trip covered before, though three runs without a win leaves a query over sealing it.

runners_data.name: Everyday Life
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced, unknown style with a finishing flag; sole run on similar going produced a ninth of 19, and Donoghue's yard form (2/16 T14) provides limited confidence — a stamina question remains unanswered.|
runners_data.comment: A repeatedly placed performer in points, she brings solid form into this sphere even though her rules debut brought only a well-beaten ninth at Downpatrick three weeks ago. There should be more to come as she adapts to hurdling, but proving that under rules remains the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Giorgia Rose
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare sporting a tongue-strap; two runs on Good going including a third over 22f suggests she stays well and should appreciate a truly-run race from behind — Emmet Mullins' yard is quiet (0/6 T14) but the profile fits.|
runners_data.comment: Having shown ability in points, she made a fair hurdles bow, only tiring up in trip when third at Tramore last time. Cheekpieces and a tongue-tie are added for the first time, and with two and a half miles suiting, there's more to come from this maiden.

runners_data.name: Glendaars Crystal
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced unknown quantity; only two runs, both on Good ground, both finishing well back — McLoughlin's yard is cold and nothing in the formbook invites confidence at this trip.|
runners_data.comment: Only two starts so far, both below the pace, most recently finishing unplaced after failing to progress from a seventh-placed hurdles debut at Punchestown. Everything remains to be proven on this scant evidence, and with little else to go on she's tricky to trust in this company.

runners_data.name: Idaho Expresso
runners_data.note: Style uncertain; a chequered recent record including unseats and a pull-up, though placed over similar ground once — trainer has only one runner in 14 days and this is a risky proposition.|
runners_data.comment: A winner in points, albeit with question marks over that form, she may need time to settle into hurdling having failed to complete at Downpatrick last time, over six weeks ago. Jumping remains the obvious query before she can be fully trusted in this sphere.

runners_data.name: Jet To Glory
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for the McConnell yard (0/27 T14 — poor form); finished fourth and fifth on Good ground over shorter, suggesting stamina for 2m4½f is unproven and a cold stable is not encouraging.|
runners_data.comment: Rock-bottom of our field, though she did show a little when fourth, beaten thirteen lengths, in a bumper at Downpatrick last time. Good ground and two miles should suit, and the yard was successful in this race last year, but there's plenty for her to find here.

runners_data.name: Jo's Secret
runners_data.note: Tongue-strap-wearing prominent type with a strong Good-ground record (4/6 similar-going runs placing) including two second places over 16f; 57 days between runs is the main risk, but A.J. Martin's yard has solid recent profile.|
runners_data.comment: Top-rated on our figures, this admirably consistent mare's hurdling form was later franked at a higher level, and she matched it when fourth, beaten seven and a half lengths, in a bumper at Downpatrick last time. Today's trip and ground are already covered, plus a first-time tongue-tie, and she rates the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Red Acres Georgie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 140 days off for Anthony Mullins; only one run on Good going (seventh) and limited hurdles experience, so the long break and sparse form make this a significant unknown despite the interesting profile.|
runners_data.comment: A winner in points but well held when tried from out in front last time, a beaten seventh in a bumper at Gowran Park. Suited by two miles two on yielding, and back from a four-month absence, there's scope for more now sent hurdling, though she has plenty to find against these.

runners_data.name: Riverwoods
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type for De Bromhead (11/35 T14 in-form); four runs on Good ground with two placed efforts including a third over 16f — handles the ground well and the in-form trainer is a key positive angle.|
runners_data.comment: Ridden more positively than before, she stayed on but faded late for a third, beaten eight and a half lengths, in a bumper at Tramore last time after a break. There's more to come with that run under her belt, and with today's ground suiting, she has claims on her best hurdling form.

runners_data.name: She's All Talk Sir
runners_data.note: No form figures available and going profile unknown; an entirely unexposed maiden with no public data — treated as a complete unknown for pace-mapping purposes.|
runners_data.comment: A daughter of Jukebox Jury on her first start, this mare is half-sister to Snap Fish, a fair performer at three miles. The yard is a little quiet currently, so she's perhaps one to note on this debut, with more to assess once she's had a run under these conditions.

runners_data.name: Star Of Idaho
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced W.P. Mullins-trained mare with an in-form yard (10/56 T14); a debut fourth over 16f on Good is the sole evidence, and 49 days since that run leaves much to prove at this longer trip.|
runners_data.comment: Fourth on her sole start, beaten nine and a quarter lengths in a bumper at Wexford, this mare is with a powerful stable and expected to progress significantly now up in trip over hurdles. Conditions look right for her, though the thin experience is the obvious question mark.

runners_data.name: Uno Me I Like My T
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a fade-in-finish flag; a troubled recent record including falls and a pull-up, and the 7lb claimer Paddy Cleary takes over — hard to trust despite the staying hold-up profile.|
runners_data.comment: Struggling to make an impression under rules, having fallen in a novice chase at Punchestown last time out. There was a place in a point beforehand, but with two recent falls and hurdles chances not yet realised, she's hard to trust in this company.

runners_data.name: Western Shores
runners_data.note: Prominent type from the in-form Gordon Elliott yard (9/43 T14); two fifth-place finishes on Good ground over 16-19f — consistent but unspectacular, and stepping up in trip could expose a stamina ceiling.|
runners_data.comment: Matched market expectations when comfortably held up in trip in a maiden hurdle at Downpatrick last time. There should be more to offer back up in distance again, with two to two and a quarter miles on good ground suiting, though two runs without troubling the judge is the query.

runners_data.name: Sonna Lady
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old with a single run (ninth of 19 on Good); the youngest runner in the field and carrying a finishing fade flag — the Hanlon yard has moderate recent form and this looks like a learning run.|
runners_data.comment: Plenty to work on after an inexperienced, error-strewn debut well beaten in a maiden hurdle at Kilbeggan, her only run to date. Time and further experience look the key requirements before she can be seriously considered in this sphere.

runners_data.name: Santa Paula
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with a consistent fade flag; three runs on relevant going all produced finishes outside the first ten, and McLoughlin's yard is out of form (0/9 T14) — stamina suspects will be exposed in a truly-run race.|
runners_data.comment: Little encouragement so far, with jumping errors contributing to a well-beaten effort in a maiden hurdle at Punchestown last time out. Nothing in the formline yet points to a change in fortunes, leaving her tricky to fancy among these on what she has shown to date.

runners_data.name: How's Ellie
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile from W.P. Mullins (9/51 T14 in-form); returning from 221 days off the track with only two runs, both fifth-place finishes — the long absence is the primary concern, though the yard will have her ready.|
runners_data.comment: Overkeen throughout and comfortably held once more in a bumper at Tramore last time, this filly is with a leading stable that may find more from her now sent hurdling. A lengthy seven-month absence adds to the queries, but a change of discipline could bring improvement over the minimum trip.

runners_data.name: Prophetess Miriam
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a solid place record (three seconds in five runs on Good ground) including efforts over this sort of trip; 27 days since last run is fine, and she clearly handles the conditions — lacks a win but profiles as a stayer.|
runners_data.comment: Overracing troubles undid her when pulling her way forward and finishing down the field in a maiden hurdle at Punchestown last time. She showed enough in bumpers to warrant a chance on that evidence, but hasn't yet translated it over hurdles, and settling remains the key issue.

races.paceDynamic: Jet To Glory and Ardeen Joy are the two confirmed front-runners in a field of 19, and with Jack Kennedy aboard Ardeen Joy and Brian Hayes on Jet To Glory, neither is likely to cede the lead without a fight — an honest, contested gallop from the outset is the most plausible outcome over this 2m4½f trip on Good ground at Bellewstown. The early duel will set a genuine pace that tests stamina throughout, and with prominent types Bold Reflection, Chisel Hill, Jo's Secret, Riverwoods, Western Shores and Prophetess Miriam all seeking to race in the first half-dozen, there is significant pressure on the early positions. Hold-up horses Giorgia Rose, Red Acres Georgie, Uno Me I Like My T and Santa Paula will be content to settle in behind the carnage, tracking a pace they have not had to create. The contested lead and honest gallop strongly favours hold-up and late-running profiles that can conserve energy in the early stages and unleash a sustained finish, with genuinely prominent types who possess a strong staying kick — rather than early pace — also in contention.

runners_data.name: Codger's Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent racer on Good ground with a placed run over similar trip at this track; Carl Millar claiming 2lb is a small bonus, and trainer Collins has a 2/18 14-day record; four Good-ground runs producing one place from four similar conditions runs, no wins — needs things to go right from the front group.|
runners_data.comment: Stepped down in grade and trip when a close second, beaten just half a length, in a maiden hurdle at Kilbeggan last time - a much better effort than his earlier starts suggested. A mixed record and top weight on a testing opening mark are the concerns, even with first-time cheekpieces added.

runners_data.name: Riyami
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has placed four times in 15 similar-going starts including a win; Denis Hogan's 2/18 14-day record is workmanlike; tongue-strap fitted, 38-day break with a fitness flag noted, and a lengthy form line of moderate finishes at this level makes it hard to see where the improvement comes from.|
runners_data.comment: A confirmed hold-up performer who races fairly off this mark, still a maiden over hurdles despite plenty of chances. His latest effort, down the field in a Flat handicap at Limerick, fell below him, but course, trip and ground are all proven, and first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces are added for this switch.

runners_data.name: Brohatna
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who has been consistently placed fourth or fifth in recent Good-ground starts; fresh on 19 days, trainer Rice has a quiet 0/2 14-day record, and no win from four similar-ground runs suggests a place prospect at best rather than a winner.|
runners_data.comment: Matched his level again when fourth, beaten seven lengths, in a maiden hurdle at Kilbeggan last time, and the opening mark looks workable on that evidence. He tends to pull hard, though, so today's longer trip is questionable, with two to two and a quarter miles on good ground his true zone.

runners_data.name: Pourquoi Poi
runners_data.note: Off-the-pace runner with a win on Good ground over 20f last time out; Kennedy claims 4lb, trip steps up slightly to 2m4½f which should suit given a placed run over 25f; eight Good-ground starts producing one win and two places makes this one of the more credible hold-up threats.|
runners_data.comment: Full of running for a long way, this gelding was outstayed up in trip in a truly run race at Punchestown last time, caught close home and beaten three and a quarter lengths off this mark. Course, trip and ground all suit, and there's more to come once switched to fences.

runners_data.name: Hurricane Honey
runners_data.note: Prominent-style handler who has placed five times from 15 similar-ground starts and recorded one win; 25 days since last run, Kevin Healy claiming 4lb, and trainer Cavanagh is 0/2 in the 14-day window — needs to bounce back from a seventh last time.|
runners_data.comment: Matched expectations before fading late, beaten eight lengths back from a break in a handicap hurdle at Sligo last time. Decent ground and two and a half miles both suit, her mark looks fair on chasing form, and that run under her belt should bring further improvement.

runners_data.name: Clone Cross
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who maps as the lone pace-setter; fell and pulled up twice in recent form but has a placed effort over 20f on Good, and Aidan Kelly is a capable pilot — the question is whether they can maintain a controlled lead without falling or fading given the fragile form profile.|
runners_data.comment: Rated among the leading threats on his maiden form, with a fair mark to boot, this gelding failed to complete at Sligo last time, though that race may have come too soon. He needs to turn that below-par effort around, but with course, trip and ground all suited, he rates highly on official figures.

runners_data.name: Hitthehayson
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins and five places from 15 Good-ground runs — among the most consistent in the field on similar going; 21 days fresh, trained by Donoghue who has a 2/16 14-day record, and the step back to a handy position off a sustainable pace suits the profile.|
runners_data.comment: Back on song when dropped in trip for a good second at Downpatrick last time, beaten four and a quarter lengths, this gelding is our top-rated runner and in good form this season. Course, trip and ground are all proven, and he rates tough to peg back, with first-time cheekpieces the only slight unknown.

runners_data.name: Soldier Saint
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a ⚠ fade-in-finish flag who has placed once from ten Good-ground starts and finished no better than fourth in the last five; Jordan Canavan claims 4lb but the profile of a horse who struggles to see out the finish is a significant negative over 2m4½f.|
runners_data.comment: Fancied to play a role but only matched his level in a well-beaten effort in a handicap hurdle at Sligo last time. Inconsistency has marked his short career so far, though today's trip and going both suit, and a first-time hood offers a fresh angle.

runners_data.name: Georginas Jet
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 18f on Good ground last time out; Jack Gilligan claiming 2lb, trainer P J Gilligan has a 1/10 14-day record, and Good ground across 12 of 14 runs with four places shows consistent handling of conditions — form is live.|
runners_data.comment: A hefty ten-length win back down in trip and off a lower mark at Downpatrick last time makes her one to respect, with a more forceful ride bringing out her best. That was a marked turnaround from a mixed run of finishes beforehand, and repeating it remains the obvious question.

runners_data.name: Poetic Focus
runners_data.note: Unclassified style with Unknown going preference shown, fades in finish flag; Josh Younge claims 4lb, trainer Slattery is 1/27 in the 14-day window which is a poor strike rate, and a run of PUF0 in recent starts makes this difficult to support.|
runners_data.comment: Overkeen and clearly needing that run back from a break, this mare was well beaten in a handicap hurdle at Limerick last time. She should strip fitter for the experience, though inconsistency has been an issue in her career and the stable is out of sorts currently, both factors against her.

runners_data.name: My Policy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from a very lengthy 436-day absence; Alix Balfe claims 4lb, and the form before the break showed two second-place finishes on Good ground — fitness is the obvious unknown and is the critical factor in any assessment of its chance.|
runners_data.comment: Showed her best form in a while when a close second at Kilbeggan last time, beaten three and a half lengths up in trip off a higher mark, though that's well over a year ago now. First-time cheekpieces and suitable ground and trip are in her favour, but the long layoff is the query.

runners_data.name: Agent Tequila
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type carrying a fade-in-finish flag; mapped to midfield here because the rear of the field will be overcrowded, but its natural preference is to come from deep which is compromised — 109-day break adds a fitness question, and a string of poor finishes including a pull-up last time out make this very hard to recommend.|
runners_data.comment: Successful in a point-to-point but yet to show much of that form under rules, failing to complete last time in a handicap chase at Wexford, needing that run after a break. He's normally held up, and today's course, trip and ground are proven, with first-time cheekpieces the fresh angle, but he still has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Fervida
runners_data.note: Unclassified style with a fade-in-finish flag and a 151-day absence; trainer Berry is 0/1 in the 14-day window, and a history of unseated, pulled-up, and mid-division finishes on a range of going types gives little confidence — risk profile is high.|
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete in a maiden hurdle at Fairyhouse last time, her jumping letting her down that day, and she's yet to show anything of real note across a mixed set of finishes. A first switch to handicaps could bring about an improvement, but proving it remains the challenge after five months on the sidelines.

runners_data.name: Ballinagaine Girl
runners_data.note: Races naturally as a hold-up type but with several hold-up runners for this trip, she's pushed into a midfield mapping where the race is unlikely to suit her best; recent form shows a second over 20f on Soft and a 14th on Good — the step to Good ground and an unfavourable position reduce her chance.|
runners_data.comment: A close second, beaten a neck off a lower mark, at Limerick last time marked a step up from her previous efforts, and she'd be a major player building further on it. Course, distance and two and a half miles are all in her favour, though repeating that level is the query.

runners_data.name: Granlahan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has placed twice from six Good-ground starts as a young 4-year-old; Patrick O'Brien claims 2lb, the 4yo allowance is worth noting in a handicap like this, and back-to-back thirds in the last two starts show a horse in form that could make the frame.|
runners_data.comment: Matched his level again with a third, beaten four and a quarter lengths, in a handicap hurdle at Sligo last time, having shown similarly the run before. He'd be dangerous building further on that pair of efforts, with course, trip and ground all suited, though the stable's current lean spell is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Clever Court
runners_data.note: Unclassified style with a fade-in-finish flag and a blinker headgear change; trainer Rothwell has a 3/30 14-day record which is poor, and a recent sequence of pull-ups and last-place finishes on a range of going types makes this one of the least reliable in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Failed to complete yet again last time in a handicap hurdle at Tramore, extending a wretched run of finishes in this grade. Blinkers are added for the first time in a bid to spark an improvement, and two to two and a half miles suits, but there's little in the formline to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Serenade
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by Gavin Cromwell who has a strong 7/41 14-day record — the trainer angle is the most positive thing about this runner; nine Good-ground runs with only one place and no wins suggests the horse has not translated potential into results, but Cromwell's form makes it one to monitor for market moves.|
runners_data.comment: Setting the pace and used up too soon, she was comfortably held in a handicap hurdle at Wexford last time. With a capable stable behind her, and course, trip and decent ground all suited, there's scope for a turnaround, but her recent run of finishes offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Lost Features
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up runner placed into midfield mapping as the rear of the field has no room; fades in finish flag and a run of 8-P-9-9-8 in recent starts on a range of ground confirms this is a consistent backmarker with no realistic route to the front — discount accordingly.|
runners_data.comment: Well beaten yet again in a handicap hurdle at Limerick last time, continuing a run of finishes that has shown little to note. Everything remains to be proven on this evidence, leaving her hard to fancy in this line-up.

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who prefers to race from the back, mapped to midfield here given the surplus of hold-up runners; trainer Hanlon has a 3/19 14-day record, three placed efforts from 15 Good-ground runs are noted, but racing out of natural role in a 19-runner field is a material negative.|
runners_data.comment: A series of jumping errors undid her last time, failing to find much in a handicap chase at Tramore and finishing well beaten. She remains a maiden despite plenty of starts, though today's course, trip and ground are all proven and first-time cheekpieces are added in search of sharper jumping.

races.paceDynamic: Clone Cross is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, with no genuine pressing rival likely to sit on their shoulder from the off, they should be able to dictate at a sustainable, controlled tempo on Good ground over 2m4½f at Bellewstown. The pace will be honest but not hot — Clone Cross sets it, Codger's Rock and Hurricane Honey likely track closely in the prominent berths, while Hitthehayson and My Policy also want to race handily. This creates a race run to a steady-to-moderate rhythm that will stretch the field and compress the gaps at the business end, putting a premium on horses that can travel within striking distance rather than those making up significant ground from deep. The field carries far more hold-up runners than can naturally settle at the rear — Mother Ship, Agent Tequila, Ballinagaine Girl, and Lost Features are all genuine hold-up types redistributed to a midfield mapping because the rear of the race will be overcrowded, meaning only the most tractable among them will find a clean route through; prominent and midfield stalkers who can travel close to the pace without over-racing are structurally best placed in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Clone Cross's jumping record — including falls and pull-ups in recent form — is a live concern at the front of a 19-runner field; if they make a serious error, the entire pace structure collapses and the race becomes unpredictable.
Whiskey Serenade is trained by Gavin Cromwell, who is 7/41 in the 14-day window — watch for a market move that might indicate this runner is sharper than the form string suggests.

My Policy returns from a 436-day absence; the pre-injury form was strong on Good ground but fitness is an unknown — monitor in the market and in the parade ring before committing to any assessment of their chance.

With several hold-up horses redistributed to midfield — Agent Tequila, Mother Ship, Ballinagaine Girl, Lost Features — watch for a bunched, congested early-middle section of the field that could cause traffic problems from the fourth hurdle onwards.

Pourquoi Poi steps up in trip to 2m4½f having placed over 25f — if the pace is genuinely slow and this runner gets a clean passage from the rear of the midfield group, the stamina profile makes them one of the most interesting late-closers in the race.

races.name: QuinnBet Bellewstown Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Lisnagar Fortune
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with Good-ground form (3rd over 20f last time), wearing headgear and trained by McConnell; strong style fit for a race where sole lead is available, though a long way back in form suggests place prospects rather than a winning finish.
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent in four runs without a win, he was well beaten at Roscommon last time, perhaps needing that outing for fitness. First-time cheekpieces and past form over today's trip and going offer some hope, but a stable short of winners and a rating of 116 leave him with work to do.

runners_data.name: Outside The Door
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old with an imposing course-and-distance profile (1W at 26f on Good, placed at 33f Good), fresh off 65 days but returns to a trip and ground that have suited well; prominent racer who should naturally slot into a productive second-row berth behind the leader.
runners_data.comment: Back on the faster ground he prefers, he confirmed his well-being when second in a cross-country chase at Punchestown latest. Now dropped to hurdles off a mark that looks lenient, with first-time blinkers and course-and-distance form on his side, he heads this at 125 after only a brief break.

runners_data.name: Burning Ability
runners_data.note: Five-year-old in good recent form (won last time at 20f on Good), trainer has one winner in the last 11 days; a natural prominent racer who could get a clean passage in the second tier and whose Good-ground record (3 runs, 1W 2P) is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Consistently in the frame this term, he won a maiden hurdle at Listowel by two lengths last time on ground he handles well, helped by a fallen rival. Handicapping now off a mark that looks lenient, he's a genuine threat at 123, with that facile scoreline the main question.

runners_data.name: Ottoman Style
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old wearing tongue-tie and blinkers, two placings at 24f on Good but zero wins at similar going in five attempts; has the style to track the pace but consistency concerns limit enthusiasm for the win.
runners_data.comment: Winless in four starts, he was eased when pulled up at Punchestown last time, with something clearly amiss. He's suited by cut but also handles decent ground, and first-time blinkers plus a tongue-tie could sharpen him, though there's plenty to prove off a rating of 116.

runners_data.name: Jisco Du Brem
runners_data.note: Won last time at 22f on Good and has multiple placings at similar conditions; wears a tongue-tie and is ridden by a 5lb claimer, but the combination of trip, going and recent form makes this one of the more interesting prominent types in the field.
runners_data.comment: Stepping up in trip and down in grade paid off when he landed a handicap by three lengths off a lower mark at Ballinrobe last time, and today's longer distance should suit him even better. On a fair mark and unfazed by cut in the ground, he's a leading threat at 118, with harder company the obvious test.

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Carries a visor and has been off 278 days — that lengthy absence is the dominant concern; has won on Good ground and shown ability, but the fitness question over 3m½f is significant after such a layoff.
runners_data.comment: Three wins from his last five starts put him in good order, though he was beaten eight lengths in a handicap at Navan last time on his first spin on the level since last spring. A yard in form and first-time visor offer some hope, but a rating of 110 leaves plenty to find here.

runners_data.name: Le Kap
runners_data.note: De Bromhead handler in strong form (6/44 over 14 days) but Le Kap has failed to place in four runs on Good, recording a best of 3rd on Soft; trip is an extension from previous starts and there is no evidence yet it will suit.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in four starts, he was comfortably held in a handicap hurdle at Clonmel last time, with that run possibly bringing him forward off a break. He handles today's ground and a rating of 111 keeps him competitive, with the form of his earlier efforts said to be working out well.

runners_data.name: Dorans Law
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type wearing tongue-tie and cheekpieces, with solid Good-ground stamina credentials (placed 2nd at 24f recently); ridden by a 7lb claimer and should get cover before making a race of it late — benefits if the pace is genuine.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts, he ran to a fair level when beaten nine lengths in a handicap hurdle at Kilbeggan last time, having had a lot of ground to make up. A good mark on his form over fences, first-time cheekpieces and tongue-tie, plus course-and-distance experience over this longer trip, work in his favour, and he's respected at 113.

runners_data.name: Radar Ahead
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who races naturally up with the pace — his form is almost entirely over shorter trips (12-13f) and he is stepping massively up in distance here; although shown in midfield on the map due to redistribution, his instinct is to race prominently and the trip looks a real test.
runners_data.comment: A mixed record over hurdles, including a win three runs back, was undermined when she parted with her jockey at Downpatrick last time, leaving her form hard to trust. She races well on good ground at shorter trips, and a rating of 111 keeps her in the mix, but the inconsistency is the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Whatsavailable
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up type wearing cheekpieces and tongue-tie, with good recent form at 24f on Good (3rd and 4th); ridden by a 5lb claimer but the patient profile suits if the pace is genuine enough to string the field out late.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in five starts, he raced too freely and was caught late when fourth, beaten 28 lengths, in a handicap hurdle at Listowel latest. He's up to today's trip and ground, and first-time cheekpieces plus tongue-tie could help settle him, with a workable rating of 110 offering a sliver of hope if his level does hold up.

runners_data.name: Midnight Moonshine
runners_data.note: By nature races with the leaders, but this crowded field means he is unlikely to secure his preferred berth — nine of his 14 Good-ground runs have produced a finish outside the top five, and recent form includes a fall and a ninth; handled here mostly as a potential spoiler rather than a winner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts, he jumped and travelled poorly, finishing down the field in a handicap chase at Tramore last time, on a track that may not have suited. Earlier form was better, and he handles decent ground up to today's trip, but a rating of 102 - bottom of this field - leaves plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: The Miracle Man
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride on this eight-year-old who has placed at 26f on Good and 22f; although his natural inclination is prominent racing, in this field he is likely to be further back than ideal — his record over hurdles shows consistent placed efforts without a win for some time.
runners_data.comment: Generally consistent without a win in five runs, he was well beaten down the field in a handicap hurdle at Sligo last time, a below-par effort after solid form before that. First-time blinkers, a notable jockey booking and course-and-distance form on ground he handles all boost his claims, with a rating of 111 keeping him in the reckoning.

runners_data.name: Mavetherave
runners_data.note: Six-year-old off 109 days and returning from a break, with Good-ground form (4th at 22f) but a modest overall win record; races with front-running instincts but will struggle to hold that position in this field and may find the stamina test on a comeback start demanding.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in easier company but yet to fire now handicapping, he was well beaten down the field in a handicap hurdle at Down Royal last time, his first try at this level. A long break since, a stayer's profile and conditions he handles offer hope, and a rating of 111 keeps him in the mix if that maiden form transfers.

runners_data.name: Justatan
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from the Emmet Mullins yard, returning after 160 days off, and all five recent runs have been over shorter distances (16-18f); the step to 3m½f looks ambitious given a tendency to finish mid-pack even over hurdles he knows.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in five starts, his first handicap proved tough, finishing down the field in a handicap hurdle at Naas last time. A long absence and a step up in trip make this a fresh test, and though a shrewd yard could find improvement, his best form has come at shorter trips, leaving him hard to fancy at 107.

runners_data.name: Tolka Row
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a tidy placed record at 22f on Good (2nd and 7th from three runs), though the form is limited in depth; front-running by nature, he is unlikely to get to the head of affairs in this company and will race below his comfort zone positionally.
runners_data.comment: Winless in five starts, he stepped forward again when upped in trip, finishing second beaten two lengths in a maiden hurdle at Tramore last time. Now sent handicapping for the first time with even further ground to travel in his favour, he could progress again, though a modest rating of 102 keeps him towards the bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Accustomed
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has a Good-ground placed record (2nd at 20f), but finishing 21st last time is a stark data point; races prominently by instinct, and the redistribution to midfield reflects an inability to impose that style in a field this size.
runners_data.comment: Rated well below his maiden form, he was ridden for the longer haul when beaten just over nine lengths in a handicap hurdle at Punchestown last time, having had too much ground to make up. Course-and-distance form, conditions he handles and first-time cheekpieces make him a big threat at 117 for all his modest mark, with a lack of a win his one query.

runners_data.name: Broken Ice
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old wearing a hood, trained by McConnell (same yard as Lisnagar Fortune), with a cluster of fourth-place finishes at 24-27f on Good; his natural inclination is to race prominently but in a field this crowded he will struggle to assert, and a win looks a stretch based on form profile.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in five starts, he lacked the gears for a shorter trip and was well held in a handicap hurdle at Wexford last time, a drop in distance that clearly didn't suit. He wants at least today's longer trip, and with course-and-distance form, first-time cheekpieces and a mark with room to rise, he has claims at 111, that below-par run perhaps bringing him forward.

races.paceDynamic: Lisnagar Fortune is the one confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field over 3m½f at Bellewstown, and with no serious challenger willing or able to match them from the outset, they are set to control a measured, sustainable gallop throughout. The pace will be genuine but not frantic — a lone leader at this distance on Good turf tends to set an honest rhythm that rewards those travelling smoothly in behind without burning energy. The field contains a significant cluster of genuine prominent types — Radar Ahead, The Miracle Man, Midnight Moonshine, Mavetherave, Tolka Row, Accustomed and Broken Ice all want to race close to the pace but cannot all hold their natural position in this shape, meaning several will be shuffled back against their will and race in unfamiliar territory. Tactically, this race shape strongly favours horses who can settle in a handy position just off the leader — true second-row prominent types and patient mid-trackers with the stamina to pick up over this marathon trip — rather than genuine hold-up horses who will have too much ground to make up off a controlled pace.
